_comment: Two version numbers, and they are independent axes. `version` is this
contract: it bumps when a rule, a threshold or a gate_io row changes.
`release.ships_with` is the release line of the skill package that
bundles this contract. The release bumps for prose and gate-behaviour
changes too, so the two only coincide when the contract happens to move.
Recorded here because nobody can tell from the numbers alone whether
1.2.4 is newer or older than 1.0.6. A deployed copy that can name both
can prove it matches the release the README describes.
1.3.1 -> 1.3.2 puts one exit_codes["2"] trigger back in its row: the
rule-set refusal, schemas/report-contract.json missing or not parseable.
1.2.4 added it together with gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set, and
the sibling key survived; the 1.2.6 rewrite of exit_codes["2"] dropped
only the wording, so a reader who trusted that flat list had lost the
earliest of the four import-time refusals. checks/contract.py reads the
JSON as its first act, and a wrong relative path is the easiest way to
reach it. No rule, no threshold and no other row moves, so the gate
behaves exactly as it did at 1.3.1: this is a documentation fix, which is
why 1.2.4's note below could call this a gap that 'needs a reader, not a
test'.
ships_with moves to 1.1.4 because the contract that ships changes, though
no gate behaviour does. A deployed copy names both numbers, and 1.1.3's
archive would otherwise carry a contract whose own table disagrees with
the row it was written to describe.
1.1.4 -> 1.1.5 moves ships_with again with no contract change at all: the
release picks up four fixes to scripts/docgen.py, which ships but is not
part of this contract, and gains the test suite that would have caught
them. _find_block_end required the subprogram name after the end keyword,
which ABAP permits but never requires, so nothing matched, every block ran
to the end of the file, and `end` came back identical for every
subprogram. CALL FUNCTION names were read from [A-Z0-9_], which missed the
quoted form that is the common one in ABAP. A FORM's USING clause was
grouped into the FORM regex with `.*?`, which matched empty, so no FORM
ever reported a parameter. Internal tables were filtered with a
case-sensitive startswith, so lt_tab and ws_data read as database tables.
The anchored patterns indented with `\s*`, which also matches a newline, so
a subprogram preceded by a blank line anchored one line early.
version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no row moved.
1.1.5 -> 1.1.6 moves ships_with again with no contract change at all: the
release picks up eight fixes to scripts/abap_deps_analyzer.py, which ships
but is not part of this contract, and makes references/example-report.md
pass the gate with its own source. row-src had never been exercised on the
exemplar, because both tests that guard it ran the gate without a source --
and row-src is the one rule that only runs when a source is passed. A third
change is in the gate's documentation, not its rules: SKILL.md's exit-code
table named eight of this contract's fifteen defect prefixes and described
--fidelity-only's output wrongly, and its exit-2 table was missing several
of the gate's refusals, including report-and-source-being-the-same-file and
the three --fix output-path refusals. version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no
threshold and no row moved.
1.1.6 -> 1.1.7 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: four fixes
to SKILL.md's prose and one to references/README.md, all found by running
the skill on two real programs. enc was in the exit-code table with no prose
anywhere, so a writer hitting a U+FFFD from a truncated multibyte character
had no way to know the fix is a re-save rather than a delete. SKILL.md claimed
both the authz and ext-asset notes go silent once the report answers them;
only authz does -- ext_asset_note returns a note whenever a bitmap or icon
literal exists, and says so in its own docstring. authz's silence bar is a
ten-keyword regex the writer could not see, so SKILL.md names it. Step 5 gains
a pre-check for those two notes, which can never be answered in steps 6 or 7
because both forbid changing the analysis and --fix only repairs ln and mm.
references/README.md now states that abap-syntax is 8 of about 30 upstream
cheat sheets, because 13 of their internal cross-links point at siblings that
were never vendored. version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no
row moved.
1.1.7 -> 1.1.8 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: the release
vendors one upstream cheat sheet and corrects the index that claimed it was
missing. The gap was real and load-bearing: SKILL.md told the writer to look
up syntax behaviour in abap-syntax and forbade inventing it elsewhere, while
references/README.md said the directory is a partial vendoring and that any
semantics absent from it are absent from it -- so a topic that fell between
had no permitted route. LOOP AT ... GROUP BY was exactly such a topic: it is
the one statement whose behaviour is defined by which binding form is used,
and 11_Internal_Tables_Grouping.md is the upstream sheet that documents the
representative and explicit key bindings, the INTO addition, GROUP INDEX and
GROUP SIZE, WITHOUT MEMBERS, and the member loop. It is now vendored, copied
verbatim, and verified against the upstream git blob SHA-1
3080642a8dba2d4f13208048c3e712a069ddbf9e, as are the other eight.
Verifying the archive instead of the working tree fails, and for a reason worth
recording: core.autocrlf=input normalised upstream's eight CRLF sheets to LF
when they were committed, so the shipped blobs do not match the upstream blobs
and only 27_Exceptions.md, already LF upstream, does. That is line-ending
normalisation, not edited content, and the index now says so -- otherwise a
reader who unpacks the release and compares would read it as tampering.
The index now names 9 of upstream's 37 sheets, records the Apache-2.0
provenance, and lists the twelve sibling files the cross-links still reach for.
Vendoring it added one new broken sibling link, 02_Structures.md, and removed
one, so the count of unique missing filenames stays at twelve. No reference
file is read by the gate, which reads only this contract, so version stays
at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no row moved.
1.3.2 -> 1.3.3 is documentation-only, and it moves version for once: every row here
describes what the gate prints, and three of them were wrong. defect_line_prefixes
named SUBSTANTIVE and PUNCT-ONLY, but report() truncates the tier with tier[:6], so
the line that starts a fidelity defect is SUBSTA and the punctuation one is PUNCT- --
a reader grepping the documented form finds nothing. exit_codes["0"] said no shape
defect was found, which is not sufficient: report() returns 0 only when not bad and
not n_sub, and n_sub counts the fidelity SUBSTANTIVE findings, which shape mode also
prints and also counts in N. A shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exits 1,
so step 7 could return 1 for a report the writer believed was done. exit_codes["1"]
said the verdict is last in shape mode; it is not -- the notes print after FAIL and
after PASS, up to seven of them, including the one announcing that five diagnostics
never ran. And advisories[fidelity] said enforcement is note, when the substantive
tier is a defect line: 1.0.8 introduced the two tiers and this row was never
updated, the same shape as the authz keyword list SKILL.md carried until 1.1.9,
where the documented list did not match the regex. Behaviour did not change, but
version moves anyway, because the wrong text is in the contract and the contract is
what a deployed copy proves itself with.
1.1.9 -> 1.1.10 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at
1.3.3, because no rule, no threshold and no row moved. One sentence in the
shipped README was wrong, and it was wrong in a way this contract's own drift
suite can never see. It called tests/test_skill.py self-contained and free of
project data, and said the same in the runbook. From the repository root that
holds, and the 169 checks the suite carried then all pass. From the installed location it does not: every
suite resolves its fixtures by walking up from tests/ to a repository root and
then looking for sibling Test-source/ and analyzing-programs-workspace/, neither
of which ships with the package. test_skill.py goes 168 of 169 there and the
one that fails is the exemplar's source-is-present check, the row-src guard,
which needs Test-source/real/. The other four die on their first fixture.
The gate itself and its scripts are unaffected: report_qc.py on the shipped
exemplar returns 0 and prints PASS from the installed location, measured.
So the 419 checks were a repository-side claim, and the README says so,
instead of implying a deployer can re-verify the release on the machine that
consumes it.
1.1.10 -> 1.1.11 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays
at 1.3.3, because no rule, no threshold and no row moved. 1.1.10 documented that
tests/ cannot run from the package; 1.1.11 stops shipping it. The harness moves
out of the archive through a NOT_SHIPPED list in release/pack.py, which asserts
a CRITICAL tuple of schemas/, scripts/, references/ and evals/ alongside it so
that putting one of those four in the exclusion list fails the pack instead of
quietly dropping a directory the gate reads. Nothing in this contract moves, and
nothing in the gate changes: the five suites were never imported by scripts/ and
read no contract key, so the archive is smaller by exactly five files and behaves
identically. Two cross-references to tests/ remain in references/README.md and
evals/README.md; they point at the repository-side suite and are left alone.
1.3.4 -> 1.3.5 moves version, because gate behaviour changes: exit 2 now
holds in every mode, not only in the shape-mode branch where its guard
had been written.
1.3.1 added the detector-crash trigger and its text says "in every mode",
and SKILL.md says so too, but the guard was added around the shape-mode
check loop and the other two branches called their detectors bare. Injecting
a RuntimeError showed --fidelity-only exiting 1 with a traceback and --fix
exiting 1 with a traceback after it had already rewritten the output file --
both read as "the check ran and found defects", which is the one false
reassurance this script exists not to give, and --fix wrote the result of an
unchecked run to disk. The guard is now run_detector(), one copy, and all
three branches go through it; putting the message in the helper is what makes
the next bare call site findable, because a per-branch copy is how this one
went undocumented.
conclusion_lines also gains PASS  <name>  (N punctuation-only): --fidelity-only
prints it when the only findings are advisory, the verdict still reads PASS and
the exit is still 0, and it was the one emittable line not on the list, so a
reader classifying output by conclusion_lines met a line the contract had never
named. exit_codes["1"] now says so, and test_skill.py constructs the case --
one space moved inside a parenthesis -- and matches the whole line, so dropping
the count is caught too.
Two rows in gate_io disagreed with the gate before 1.3.5, and neither is wrong
about anything a reader needs: source_is_optional.verdict_still_printed said
"three diagnostics" where the note and needs_source say five, and
diagnostics.enforcement said "note -- never changes the exit code" while
advisories[fidelity].enforcement says its SUBSTANTIVE tier does. The second is
the drift that matters: fidelity is listed under diagnostics, so read straight
through it reads as advisory only. Both are corrected, and enforcement now
names the exception instead of ignoring it.
ships_with moves to 1.1.13: the gate behaves differently, so a deployed copy
that names 1.3.4 is carrying the hole.
1.3.3 -> 1.3.4 moves version, because gate behaviour changes: --fix now returns 1
for a substantive rewrite, not only for the shape defects it left behind.
fidelity_report() was already being called in the --fix branch, but n_sub fed only
the notes, and the return was `1 if left else 0` where left is the shape check -- so
a shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exited 0 and printed PASS out of
--fix while exiting 1 with a FAIL out of shape mode. exit_codes["0"] already said a
rewrite blocks 0, so this contract and the gate disagreed, and step 7 loops on the
exit code, so the loop could stop on a fabricated quote.
The fidelity computation moved above the verdict; the note order did not move, which
is what notes_follow_the_verdict below asserts and test_contract_drift.py pins. The
verdict now names the two kinds separately rather than one count, so a reader can tell
that nothing mechanical was left versus that a quote still needs the model.
ships_with moves to 1.1.12: the gate behaves differently, so a deployed copy that
names 1.3.3 is carrying the hole.
1.3.0 -> 1.3.1 adds one exit_codes["2"] trigger: an unhandled exception in
a detector. It arrived with 1.1.3, which fixes inventory() for the event
blocks -- ANCHORS gives the six of them no capture group because the
keyword is the name, and inventory() took group 1 from every entry, so any
report checked against the 17 shipped sources that declare one crashed with
a traceback and exited 1, the defect verdict. Step 7 loops on a nonzero
exit, so the model edited a report whose defects did not exist. The check
loop now refuses through die(), the way the rule set and the checks import
already did. ships_with moves to 1.1.3 because gate behaviour changed; the
1.1.2 archive still carries this contract at 1.3.0.
1.1.3 also corrects a mislabel: the 1.1.2 archive declares version 1.1.1 in
its own SKILL.md frontmatter, so a deployed copy could not prove it was
1.1.2 by reading itself.
1.2.6 -> 1.3.0 adds five rule keys and nothing else changes:
problem_section.rows_require_source_object, layers.distinct,
encoding.replacement_char, mermaid.required_diagrams and
sections_exactly_once. They were declared before the detectors that
read them, so a reader of 1.3.0 alone would have believed the gate was
unchanged; they are all enforced now, as row-src, layer-same, enc,
mm-missing and sec-dup. Declaring a threshold before the detector is
the point -- the drift suite can prove the key is present and named,
which is a claim about the contract, and separately that a detector
reads it, which is a claim about the gate. The first was impossible to
state while the key did not exist.
1.2.6 -> 1.3.0 also fills the two exit_codes["2"] rows that splitting
report_qc.py into checks/ created and this file did not record:
scripts/checks/ absent, and a module in it that will not parse. Both
refuse before main() and both print an `error` line, which is the whole
reason they have to arrive through the same door as the rule-set
refusal. The gate and the table below now say the same thing.
1.0.6 -> 1.0.7 changed no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row, so
this contract stayed at 1.2.4 and only ships_with moved. Both fixes
came from field reports on another machine: the three layers
rendered as one paragraph because SKILL.md's own compact example put
them on consecutive lines, and the first layer came out too vague to
be useful. Neither was mechanically detectable, so the drift test
had nothing to assert there either.
1.2.5 -> 1.2.6 changes no rule, no threshold and no advisory. It rewrites
exit_codes["2"] to match the gate, because that one string was the last
place where a claim about the checker had never been measured. Three
wrongnesses: it said every trigger prints a line starting with `error`
while two of them print no such line; it listed `source is empty` with no
mode, so a reader would refuse a plain-mode run that in fact takes a note
and returns the shape verdict; and it identified the gate by byte size,
which made the sentence go stale every time the file grew. The per-mode
table in SKILL.md was checked cell by cell -- all 13 agree -- and it is
the one to trust. The byte sizes are gone on purpose.
1.2.4 -> 1.2.5 adds two advisories, so that version does move. They
came out of a held-out run (zvend, 21 frozen defects, blind judging)
in which the with_skill arm lost 5 defects to the without_skill arm
and every one of them was the same shape: the report NAMED the
identifier -- a hardcoded bitmap, an IS NOT INITIAL on a range, a
missing AUTHORITY-CHECK -- and then wrote a descriptive sentence and
moved on. The code was read; the conclusion was not followed through.
No gate check can catch that, so these are notes: they put the
question in front of the writer rather than asserting a defect. Both
stay silent once the report states a consequence, because naming the
topic is not answering it.
1.2.3 -> 1.2.4: exit_codes["2"] gained the rule-set trigger, and
gate_io.gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set was added. report_qc.py
already refused; SKILL.md already taught it. The contract, which this
file exists to be the single copy of, was the only place still missing
it. test_contract_drift.py cannot catch that class of gap -- it only
asserts that skill_anchor strings appear in SKILL.md -- so a drift this
wide needs a reader, not a test.
1.3.5 -> 1.3.6 moves version, because the checks that read a source read a
file of blanks as a real one. report_qc.py tested not src.strip() while the
six source-dependent checks tested not src, so a truthy string of blanks
reached them: classify() counted zero identifiers and called every quotation
a fabrication, and row-src computed an empty flat_src instead of None, which
bypassed its own "no source given: cannot judge, so do not fail" hatch and
reported every problem row as naming nothing. The exemplar plus a blank
source printed 28 defects and exited 1, while --fidelity-only refused the
same file -- three modes, three answers for one input. What could not be
judged was reported as a judgement, the false verdict the ReadError guard
exists to stop. checks/text.py gained _src_of(), one normalisation all three
modules already import from.
Two rows also disagreed with the note. skip_note listed five checks that were
not run and needs_source listed the same five, while row-src is a sixth that
needs a source and is skipped with them; 1.3.5 caught three against five and
left the sixth out. Both are six now, and row-src is the one enforced check
in needs_source -- the rest are advisories, which is why it is named.
ships_with moves to 1.1.14: a deployed copy that names 1.3.5 scores a blank
source as 28 defects.
1.3.6 -> 1.3.7 moves version for two things that were each one line and both
leaving a documented promise untrue. The fidelity note counted its own
mismatches and nothing else, so a reader could not tell three rewrites in a
long report from three in a short one; and three in a short one is where the
note could not tell "the report rewrote the code" from "the wrong source
file was passed" -- the exemplar plus a comments-only file, an English prose
file or an unrelated program all printed the same verdict as a fabricated
report. The note now reads N of M, M every quoted statement in the report,
and only M equal to the number of SUBSTANTIVE findings adds the question, because that
is the one boundary that needs no threshold: a cutoff on identifier count
would not separate the cases, since a comments-only file yields 6 identities

and an English prose file 20, both non-zero. 1.3.8 corrects this comment: it said mismatches, and the code that shipped did count the mismatches -- sub plus PUNCT-ONLY -- so the note asked whether the source was the wrong file in the one configuration that proves it is the right one, because a quotation matched it in its meaningful tokens. The comment is the one place that described the shipped bug as correctness. classify() returns only the
mismatches, so both halves now read _quote_probes() instead.
Die() indented its refusal two spaces while the two import-time refusals
printed it flush left, so the same refusal arrived three different ways and
SKILL.md's "the output begins with error" was untrue for every refusal that
goes through die(). All three now start at column 0, which is also what
conclusion_lines already recorded. ships_with moves to 1.1.15.
1.3.8 moves version because a refused --fix changed what exit 2 meant, and because the gate began to refuse where it used to raise.

A --fix write that could not happen raised OSError and printed a traceback with exit 1. Exit 1 is what a caller loops on, and the caller went looking for defects that had never been found: the write sat outside run_detector(), the guard the four detectors got in 1.1.3. No test could reach it, because the pre-flight check covered -o's directory and never -o itself. Now write_text() refuses through die(), and the message says nothing was written and that the run is not a verdict -- not that nothing was inspected, because the report was read first.

--fidelity-only took several reports and validated them inside its loop, so it printed a PASS and then refused. Plain mode pre-validates. Now it does too, and exit 2 can no longer follow a printed verdict.

The fidelity hint in 1.3.7 fired when every quotation was a mismatch of either kind, but it meant SUBSTANTIVE: PUNCT-ONLY is a quotation whose tokens do occur in the source, so the sentence said not one quotation matches in the configuration that proves the source is right. Measured: a punctuation-only quotation plus a substantive one printed 1 of 2 rewrite the source, and not one quotation matches. Note that the 1.3.7 comment above recorded the correct boundary -- mismatches -- and is what 1.3.8 corrects, so the wrong text sat in the record of the fix.

A quotation longer than the thirty-token identity window was always SUBSTANTIVE even when verbatim in the source: the window set could not see it, and the union rule in classify() turned that silence into a rewrite. Measured over 81 sources and 177092 statements, 8 were longer than the cap, longest 40 tokens -- and every one of them was a SUBSTANTIVE that never cleared, so steps 6 and 7 looped on a defect that does not exist. Those probes are now searched directly.
A directory passed as the source reported itself as a file that is not utf-8, which is a PermissionError wearing an encoding error's clothes, and sent a reader hunting for a BOM in a folder.

ships_with moves to 1.1.16: a deployed copy that names 1.3.7 scores the same refusals as tracebacks and exit 1, and it scores the wrong boundary in advisories[1]. note_counts_its_denominator. The same gap the 1.3.5 note names for a copy that names 1.3.4.

1.3.10 moves version because the gate's exit-2 pre-flight widened from existence to readability, and because one recorded refusal named only one role. A report that is a directory, or that does not decode as utf-8, used to be refused inside the loop after the earlier reports had printed their verdict, so exit 2 could follow a printed PASS that SKILL.md promised would never happen; both are now checked before any report is read, in every mode. The trigger set did not move, so nothing was added to exit_codes[2] and nothing changed in the SKILL.md rule table. directory_as_source.prints now carries both the report form and the source form where only the source form stood, so the report form a reader looked up actually resolves. ships_with moves to 1.1.18.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.20 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. A new shipped script, scripts/recon.py, covers Analysis Flow steps 1 and 2 in one call: it checks the source, prints it numbered, then runs docgen as a child and reads back the file docgen wrote, so the encoding check, the numbered source and the subprogram inventory arrive in one round instead of three. The inventory previously needed its own round because docgen prints a four-line receipt to stdout and writes the inventory to a file. recon.py exits only 0 and 2, never 1: it does not judge the report, so it has nothing to report as a defect, and a caller that treats every nonzero exit as defects found would hunt for defects that were never checked. Every refusal prints an error line before anything else, so a refusal cannot be preceded by a partial dump that reads like a verdict. It locates docgen by its own path, so it does not require the current directory to be the skill root the way report_qc.py does. The extraction stays in docgen, which is what a report is written against, so the two cannot diverge. No gate check touches recon.py and nothing in this contract describes it, which is why version does not move.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.21 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. tests/test_skill.py grew from 241 to 283 checks, and the 42 new ones are for scripts/recon.py, which shipped at 1.1.20 with nothing in any suite touching it. They pin the exit-code domain to 0 and 2, the six refusals each with an error line before any source, the numbering against the source line it labels, the byte count against the character count, the carriage return as preserved, the inventory against the file docgen wrote, and both docgen outcomes by running a stub in docgen's place. Two of the new checks failed on first run, and both failures were recon's own defects rather than the tests. One is here: recon printed its dump through a stdout that Windows translates, so every dump line ended with a carriage return whether or not the source had one, and a dump line read byte for byte carried a character the source never had. report_qc reads the source without translating newlines, so the dump and the gate disagreed on the same line; recon now reconfigures its streams to stop translating, so the terminator is identical on every platform. The other is a limit the tests record rather than close: recon's guard that docgen wrote its file only proves that a file exists at that path, so a stale one left there by an earlier run into the same output directory satisfied it and recon reported success. Nothing in the gate changed, which is why version does not move.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.22 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. scripts/recon.py now runs docgen before it writes the dump, so every refusal arrives before anything is printed. Before this a refusal after the source checks -- docgen refused, or docgen reported success without writing its file -- had already sent the whole numbered source out, so a reader had spent a full context on a run that turned out to be a refusal. The same move is what makes the total byte count in the header knowable at all, which is why the header reports it: the reader can weigh how much of the context the run spent. The number carries no rule about which path to take, which is what references/large-inputs.md already records. tests/test_skill.py grew from 283 to 287 checks: the header total is compared against the byte count that actually went out, the byte count is kept apart from the character count, and a docgen refusal now has to leave no numbered line behind. That third one is the check the 1.1.21 suite did not have, which is why the defect went unnoticed. Nothing in the gate changed, which is why version does not move.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.23 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. Four defects the 1.1.22 release had no test for. First, recon.py promised in its own docstring that there is no exit 1 -- it does not judge the report, so it has nothing to report as a defect, and a caller that treats every nonzero exit as defects found would hunt for defects that were never checked. The promise had a hole: the file docgen wrote was read back with an unguarded read_text(), so a docgen that wrote bytes that are not utf-8 raised UnicodeDecodeError out of the script, printed a traceback, and exited 1. Measured: rc=1, Traceback, and the first line was not error. A refusal was arriving in the form of a crash, which is the failure shape SKILL.md defines as the defect verdict. Every read is now guarded, and the size of what docgen wrote comes from the bytes already in hand instead of a second stat(), so there is no second look at a path that can change under the read. Second, recon never checked that docgen was installed, so a missing docgen became python's own exit 2 for a script it cannot open, and recon reported docgen exited 2 -- an exit code for a docgen that never ran, which sent a reader after a diagnosis that does not exist, and dropped the stderr that said why. Third, recon echoed docgen's stdout but not its stderr, so a docgen that crashed left the exit code as the only account of what happened; both streams are now echoed, after the error line, so the error line stays first. Fourth, report_qc.py reported a file that exists but cannot be read as is not readable as utf-8: read_report and read_src both caught (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) and printed the pair as one, which sent a reader to fix the encoding of a file that was fine and unreadable for another reason. The two clauses are now separate, so a denial reads as a denial. The trigger set did not move, so nothing was added to exit_codes[2], and directory_as_source.why_not_encoded was updated to match, because it described the OSError clause as saying is not readable as utf-8, which it no longer does; the directory check stays, because cannot be read says what failed but not what to do. One output label moved as well. recon's block header said SUBPROGRAM INVENTORY (scripts/docgen.py --type onboarding), naming the subprogram table inside, but the block docgen writes is a developer onboarding guide whose subprogram table is one of seven sections: measured 1334 bytes, 0 lines containing FUNCTION, 6 of the 7 headings unrelated to this program, and 956 bytes -- 72 to 73 percent -- byte-identical between two different programs. The header now says DOCGEN OUTPUT, and the size in the summary line says docgen block, so the label names what docgen wrote without colliding with the receipt's docgen wrote ... (N bytes), which is the file on disk and is larger because the block drops its trailing whitespace. tests/test_skill.py grew from 287 to 311 checks. Four of the new ones failed on first run. Three were the tests: a docgen stub's escapes needed one more layer of parsing, because the stub body is the source of another script, so \xff in the test became the raw byte 0xff there and the stub died with a syntax error; a comparison of text with bytes, which can never be true; and an expectation that docgen's receipt would be echoed when docgen had exited 0, which recon does not echo. The fourth found recon's own defect: the header total was compared against the byte count of text=True output, which translates the carriage returns docgen put in its own markdown, so the total recon claimed sat 41 bytes above what the test read. The wire carried the 1635 recon claimed, and the CRLF test further down already read the wire for the same reason -- which is how the suite measured the dump in bytes and the header in translated text. Nothing in the gate changed, which is why version does not move.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.24 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. Nine defects the 1.1.23 release had no test for: four were a refusal arriving in the form of a crash, three were the wrong account of a failure that had not crashed, one was prose, and one is recorded here unfixed. First, recon.py read docgen with text=True, encoding="utf-8" and no errors=, so a child that emitted bytes that are not utf-8 made child.stdout come back None, and child.stdout + child.stderr raised TypeError: rc=1, an empty stdout, and the first line was not error. docgen.py has been given the stream reconfigure its two siblings already had, and recon decodes the child with errors="replace", so child.stdout can never be None. Second, a rule set that parses but carries no sections raised KeyError in checks/contract.py at the derivation that follows the load: exit 1, the code a real defect verdict gets, for a rule set that was merely reshaped. The top-level keys are now checked inside the same try, and the catch widens to KeyError and TypeError, so every shape json.load can return is refused by the rule-set guard with the wording that trigger already promised. Third, evaluate.py assumed the reference and the verdicts had the shapes it was written against: an array at the root hit d.get, a defect entry that was a scalar hit x.get, and a verdict value that was a list was used as a dict key, all three tracebacks at exit 1. Each is now named. Fourth, the contract load in docgen.py caught (OSError, JSONDecodeError) and not UnicodeDecodeError, so a contract that exists but is not utf-8 escaped the guard as a traceback; ValueError covers both, JSONDecodeError being a subclass of it. The wrong accounts. Fifth, _read_source in docgen.py caught (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as one clause, so a source that exists and cannot be read was announced as one that is not utf-8: the misdiagnosis report_qc.py fixed at 1.1.23, in the third reader with the same two-clause shape. The clauses are separate. Sixth, recon passed -o to docgen and let the failure of docgen be the diagnosis of a path recon owns; it now pre-flights its own flag and names it. Seventh, a source with no printable character at all passed .strip(), because .strip() removes whitespace and not control bytes, so a file of null bytes was accepted as a one-line program and got a document about a program that does not exist; recon.py and docgen.py now ask for a printable character. Eighth, prose alone: SKILL.md still called the block docgen writes an inventory, so a reader who looked for == SUBPROGRAM INVENTORY looked for a header that stopped shipping at 1.1.23; it names DOCGEN OUTPUT and says the subprogram table is one of the seven sections docgen writes. Ninth, the one left unfixed: the receipt in recon.py echoes the output path it was given, so "output N bytes" counts a number that moves with the length of that path, while the docgen block count in the same line does not. The total is honest about what it counts, and only its invariance is missing; the count a reader needs to check is the one that does not move, so it is recorded rather than changed. One script still decodes a source with errors=ignore in two places, and two scripts still lack the stream reconfigure; neither is reachable from a refusal, so neither is touched. The trigger set did not move, so nothing was added to exit_codes["2"]; the refusals that were tracebacks at 1.1.23 are the same refusals, arriving as refusals. tests/test_skill.py grew from 311 to 365 checks and the five suites from 612 to 666. Nothing in the gate changed, which is why version does not move.

1.3.11 -> 1.1.26 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.11, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. Two scripts that ship now reconfigure their own streams, the same guard report_qc.py, recon.py and docgen.py have carried since 1.1.0, 1.1.20 and 1.1.24. The reason they were left out is recorded in the 1.1.24 note above and it was wrong: it says they are not subprocesses that another script reads, so the encoding failure cannot reach them. It is reachable from their own stdout. abap_deps_analyzer.py prints a Chinese report, so on a console whose codepage has no CJK -- cp936, the default on a Chinese Windows, or cp437 -- print() raised UnicodeEncodeError inside the try that catches Exception, the handler printed its error line and exited 2. Exit 2 is refused, nothing was checked, for a run that had finished its analysis: the caller was told the tool never ran when it ran and produced its findings, and the findings never reached it. Measured on one source, unchanged by this release: rc=0 under the default encoding, rc=2 under cp437 and cp936 before, rc=0 under all three after. Under cp936 the partial output that did get out was itself garbled, so the one line that arrived could not be read either. A shape of the same defect was already repaired once, in a way that only hid it: at 1.1.10 the handler printed its prefix in Chinese, so under cp437 the handler crashed on its own prefix, the traceback replaced the diagnosis, and the exit was 1, the code for the analysis ran and found defects, for a report that was never produced. Making that prefix ASCII stopped the traceback and left the exit code wrong, which is how the defect survived to 1.1.26. evaluate.py takes the same guard although its own source has no non-ASCII at all: its tasks command prints the anchors and identifiers out of the defect reference a human supplies, and that file is whatever language its author wrote it in. Neither script is named by this contract's gate_io, which is why version does not move. tests/test_skill.py grew from 396 to 399 checks: the assertion guarding the reconfigure covered docgen.py and recon.py only, and report_qc.py, which has had it since 1.1.0, was never asserted at all, so the loop now names all five scripts. The five suites are at 742 checks.

1.3.12 -> 1.3.13 adds one rule, escape_residue, and one defect kind, esc, because a report can be valid UTF-8 and still carry an escape written out as text: the writer owed one newline and typed the two characters. One shipped report carried nine of them, all nine the same shape, and the file was otherwise clean -- valid UTF-8, six sections, three layers, four buckets -- so every existing detector passed it and a reader got a report that read as a rendering fault in its own prose. enc already covers the half where the bytes are wrong; this covers the half where the bytes are right and the writer escaped a character that was meant to be the character. --fix does not repair it, for the same reason it does not repair enc: the fix is one line of intent rather than a substitution, and a repair that guessed where the newline belonged would have invented prose. The rule ships with a scope and not only a pattern: tick-n runs on prose outside code fences, and backslash escapes run on prose outside fences and outside inline backtick spans, because a quoted \n is the writer naming the escape rather than shipping one, and a Windows path carries a backslash n that is not an escape either. Measured before it shipped -- the tick-n shape had zero hits in 197 markdown files, and the backslash shape hit only this repository's own release log, which the gate never reads -- and the first tick-n pattern caught only one of the five residue shapes, which is why the measured pattern below is the second one -- so a copy that names 1.3.12 lets this through and one that names 1.3.13 does not. ships_with moves to 1.1.29.

1.3.11 -> 1.3.12 moves version, because the gate's --fix write changed what a backup is owed for and one trigger widened. A backup was owed by the guard `if dest == rep and n`: only when the report was rewritten in place, and only when something had been repaired. That guard did not match the promise fix_writes_a_backup made, which covers -o as well. Measured on one source: a 33-byte file named by -o became the 889-byte repaired report, repaired was printed, the exit was 0, and there was no .bak anywhere -- the pre-flight covered the directory of -o and never -o itself, which is why no test could reach it either. The guard is now a byte comparison, old_bytes != written, so a backup is owed whenever the write would lose something: in place, or via -o, or when a repair that found nothing replaces a foreign file with the report, because those bytes are the file's own and the write loses them. A no-op --fix writes back the same bytes and owes none, which is the property that makes an in-place --fix safe to run twice. A .bak that already held a version was overwritten too: two in-place runs, each repairing something, left 833 bytes at .bak and then 829, with no .bak.2 and no warning, so the copy that had survived the first repair was the one lost. It refuses now, file or directory, on the trigger exit_codes[2] already carried, so the row widened rather than gaining one. And the restore of the report's own endings was a boolean that asked whether a CRLF appeared anywhere: a report with one CRLF among fifty-five LFs came out with fifty-six CRLFs and no lone LF, and the receipt read repaired 0 mechanical defect(s). Each break is carried back to its own position instead of one style being chosen for the document, so the receipt and the file agree by construction and no wording had to change -- SKILL.md already promised the endings would be preserved, and the code does it now. ships_with moves to 1.1.27. tests/test_skill.py grew from 399 to 416 checks and the five suites from 742 to 759.

1.3.13 -> 1.1.30 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.13, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. The packer lost the exclusion that keeps the test harness out of a release, and the verifier could not see it. 1.1.29 shipped eleven files under tests/ -- the whole harness -- and still passed --verify at 461 entries, because ship() and verify() walked a tree filtered by the same exclusion, and that exclusion had been dropped when the packer was rewritten. Every suite under tests/ resolves its fixtures by walking up to a repository root and reading sibling Test-source/ and analyzing-programs-workspace/, neither of which ships, so outside the repository tree four suites die on their first fixture with FileNotFoundError and two fail one assertion each; inside it the walk happens to reach a real root and everything reads green, which is how the defect sat. The exclusion is back as NOT_SHIPPED, with a CRITICAL assertion that refuses to let it overlap the paths the gate reads in either prefix direction, matched against the path relative to the walked root rather than the arcname -- every arcname is prefixed with the package directory name, so matching it against the arcname would never have fired. verify() now checks a release against NOT_SHIPPED on an unfiltered walk: a verifier that walked the filtered tree would find a polluted release self-consistent, since the directory really does hold those files, which is the exact shape that hid this. 1.1.29 is not repaired -- release/ is append-only and its recorded digest is valid for the zip it names, which is the one that carries the harness. Nothing in the gate moved, which is why version does not move.

1.1.30 -> 1.1.31 moves ships_with and moves the contract with it, to 1.3.14, because one rule was added and one violation_kinds row was added. The first layer was the one rule in this skill the gate had explicitly declined to enforce, and it had declined it in the skill's own words: SKILL.md said the gate checks only that the labels exist and that the window holds more than twenty characters, and that this layer is the writer's alone. It was also the rule that had already been written down in full -- 展开成带编号/字段/条件的清单，不要一句话概括, with the four questions 取什么 / 怎么驱动 / 条件是什么 / 写到哪里 and three 反对/赞成 pairs -- and then skipped twice inside one session. The writer read all four bullets and all three pairs in the same conversation that produced a report whose every first layer came back as a single paragraph. A rule that only prose carries loses to a rule a machine reads, and the second failure is the evidence: the rule was on screen when the paragraph was written. So the shape became checkable, and only the shape. A8-list fires when the first layer's body carries fewer list items than the quoted block has statements -- fewer than single_statement_items for a block of one statement, fewer than items_min_per_block for anything larger -- where an item is a line starting with a circled digit, a markdown ordered marker, or a markdown bullet. The denominator is _statements(): non-blank, non-comment lines of the block with FORM/ENDFORM/FUNCTION/ENDFUNCTION, the START-OF-SELECTION header and the block closers dropped. That split exists because a block that does one thing cannot be asked for two items without inventing prose, while a block that does five has to be enumerated to be described at all. What the gate still cannot see is written in this block's own why field: one item covering ten statements passes. That stays with the writer, and it is the same boundary the skill already drew for 笼统 -- the list makes a missing condition visible as a missing item, it cannot say whether the item that is present is specific enough. test_contract_drift.py is unchanged and still fails when a rule carries no anchor in the skill, so the anchor 展开成带编号/字段/条件的清单，不要一句话概括 was left in SKILL.md verbatim rather than paraphrased. The reference report was rewritten to comply: its five first layers were the most substantive prose in that document and all five are now lists, so the shape the gate now demands is the shape the exemplar already demonstrated.

1.3.14 -> 1.1.32 moves ships_with and moves the contract with it, to 1.3.15, because A8-list's accepted marker set narrowed. The rule shipped at 1.1.31 counting circled digits U+2460-U+246B as list items, and a report written to that rule -- one circled digit per line, exactly as SKILL.md's own examples showed -- passed the gate and then printed as a single paragraph. A circled digit is an ordinary CJK character, not a markdown list marker: CommonMark merges consecutive plain lines into one paragraph, so the gate had validated a shape that renders as nothing. It did so because SKILL.md had called ① ② ③ 'markdown 有序列表编号'. The accepted set is now the one markdown actually renders -- `1.` / `1)` ordered, `-` / `*` / `+` bulleted, at a line start -- and the full-width 1。 / 1、 endings are out too, for the same reason. do_what gains a markers field recording which characters count and why the circled digits are not among them; nothing else about the rule moved, so items_min_per_block, single_statement_items and _statements() as the denominator stay where the previous note set them. SKILL.md's three 赞成 examples were rewritten from circled digits to 1. because they were the pattern a writer copies, the reference report's first layers and the shipped report's sixteen became ordered lists with wording unchanged apart from the marker, and test_gate_enforcement.py's listify() now emits numbered markers so the derived baseline still complies. PROBE 11 is the regression for this exact defect: it takes the compliant baseline, swaps its markers back to circled digits one per line, and asserts the gate rejects the result.
Machine-readable contract for what a report must contain.
This file is the source for report_qc.py's rules about report shape: which
sections, which layer labels, which priority buckets, which citation spellings
are forbidden, which Mermaid characters break a label, and how far a prose
window reaches. The checker reads them rather than hardcoding patterns, so
none of those can exist in the checker alone. ABAP construct syntax (the
ANCHORS table) stays in the checker: it describes the source, not the report,
and it is the list a repair is allowed to substitute. Each rule carries a
`skill_anchor`: a token that must also appear in
SKILL.md. test_contract_drift.py fails when a rule has no anchor in the
skill, or the skill states a constraint no rule covers.
Why this exists: seven separate fixes in this project were a checker
detector disagreeing with the rule it was supposed to enforce. LINENO
matched two spellings so `L23` scored clean; the Mermaid pattern differed
between the checking half and the fixing half; the exemplar's own snippet
guard had a quote-exemption the skill never granted. A second copy of the
rules inside the checker is the cause, so there is now only this one.

1.3.10 -> 1.1.19 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at 1.3.10, because no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row moved. What moved is that the gate began to honour a rule it already had. checks/tokens.py let a string literal cross a newline -- the literal alternative was "'(?:[^']|'')*'" and [^'] also matches a line feed -- so one unmatched apostrophe in a comment opened a literal that swallowed every statement after it until the next apostrophe. For zalvtree.abap the identity dropped from 635 tokens to 429, with APPEND going 12 to 1 and fieldcatalog 20 to 2. Sixty-six of the 150 verbatim quotations in the report read as SUBSTANTIVE rewrites; read back against the source, all 150 are byte-identical and not one is a rewrite. The tier is decided by identity alone, so the flattened-substring half of classify() could not rescue them, and the exit code said 1 where it said 0: a report the writer believed was honest read as fabricated. The literal may no longer cross a newline -- an ABAP statement ends in a period and a comment runs to the end of the line, so a quote closes on the line it opened on -- and '' still counts as one literal. Two checks guard it, and the first fails on the code that preceded the fix. ships_with moves to 1.1.19: a deployed copy that names 1.1.18 reports rewrites that were never written, wherever a comment contains an apostrophe.

1.1.25 moves ships_with and moves the contract with it, to 1.3.11, because two gate_io rows changed: the rule-set trigger now names a rule that is present and mistyped, and exit_codes[2] now names a source with no analysable character instead of only an empty one. Three crashes and one silent false PASS, all in the shape of a rule set or a source that parses into something the code does not expect. First, a report contract that parses can still be unusable: json.load accepts {"version": "1.3.10"}, which has a version and none of the rules. 1.1.24 moved the derivations under the guard and recorded that the catch widened to cover every shape json.load can return. It did not: the presence loop and the derivations were two separate try blocks, so a rule that was present and mistyped died outside the guard, in exceptions the clause did not name -- StopIteration from advisories with no density row, LookupError from a problem section that is also the last section, re.error from a pattern the contract supplies that does not compile, and TypeError from the joining. Each exited 1 with a traceback, the defect verdict, for a rule set that was only reshaped. The derivations now sit inside the guard and the catch names the four, so the third state refuses on the same error line as the first two. Second, the twin schema had no presence or shape loop at all: docgen.py refused an unreadable docgen-contract.json, but a contract that parsed into a root object with no rules answered PASS against no required sections and no flags -- a verdict with nothing behind it, which is the one false reassurance --validate exists not to give. Presence and shape are now checked in the same call as the read, so a mistyped contract refuses at the contract instead of raising AttributeError out of validate(). Third, the source-content predicate existed in four places and three of them disagreed: .strip() removes whitespace and not control bytes, so a source of 500 null bytes passed and the gate scored the report against it, reporting fidelity defects that were never defects; and isprintable() is True of U+FFFD, the replacement character, so a source that was nothing but the corruption signature the encoding rule exists to catch also passed, and a document was generated about a program that does not exist. Both are one predicate now, has_content() in checks/source.py, which imports no rule set so docgen.py and recon.py can read it without taking on report-contract.json with it -- that was the first attempt and it made docgen refuse on the report contract's words, which is a refusal about the wrong file. recon.py keeps a fallback for the one layout the stub tests run it in, recon.py beside nothing but docgen.py, and a test compares the two on the same inputs so they cannot drift. The messages aligned with the predicate: recon already said no analysable content, and report_qc and docgen said is empty, so all three now say the same thing for the same condition. tests/test_skill.py grew to 396 checks, from 365, and tests/test_docgen_deps.py to 171, from 129: five mistyped rules, six mistyped docgen contracts, both source shapes, and the recon fallback predicate that must not drift. schemas/docgen-contract.json moves to 1.0.3 with this release for the same guard, and its ships_with moves off 1.1.19.

1.1.27 moves ships_with and moves the contract with it, to 1.3.12, because two gate_io rows changed: fix_writes_a_backup names the guard that was actually written, and exit_codes[2] names a backup that is a file as well as a directory. Three defects in --fix, the only mode that writes, none of which the 1.1.26 release had a test for. First, an -o that named an existing file destroyed it: the pre-flight covered the directory of -o and never -o itself, and no backup was owed because the guard was `if dest == rep and n`. Measured, 33 bytes becoming 889, repaired printed, exit 0, no .bak anywhere. A backup is now owed whenever the write would lose something, decided by comparing bytes, which covers the -o half and the case where a repair that found nothing still replaces a foreign file. Second, a .bak that already held a version was overwritten without a word, so the copy that had survived the first repair was the one lost; it refuses now, file or directory, on the trigger exit_codes[2] already carried, so the row widened rather than gaining a trigger. Third, the receipt said it had repaired nothing while the file changed: the restore of the report's own endings asked only whether a CRLF appeared anywhere, so one CRLF among fifty-five LFs became fifty-six CRLFs and no lone LF, under a receipt that read repaired 0 mechanical defect(s). Each break is carried back to its own position, so the receipt and the file agree by construction. SKILL.md's --fix promises did not move -- preserve the report's own endings was already written, and the code does it now -- which is why the row that moved is the guard, not the promise. One finding is recorded unchanged: three of the eleven keys this contract checks for presence are not read by the gate, gate_io, loop_position and claim_separation, so they are documentation the checker never enforces. That is a question about what belongs in a contract, not a crash, so it stays recorded rather than changed. tests/test_skill.py grew from 399 to 416 checks and the five suites from 742 to 759.
