layers.exempt: fence language only -- an abap-fix fence illustrates a proposed fix and needs no layers
layers.skill_anchor: 每个代码块后三层都必须出现
layers.prose_window: from the closing fence to the next fence of any language or the next heading -- not to the next quoted fence, which let labels inside an intervening abap-fix fence, or the label words anywhere later in the document, satisfy a block that had no prose of its own
layers.distinct_why: three layers carrying one sentence is a list, not an analysis; the labels exist but say nothing

do_what.label: LAYERS[0], the first layer
do_what.shape: a real markdown list -- `N.` / `N)` ordered or `-`/`*`/`+` bulleted, one item per action, each item stating what is taken, how it is driven, what the condition is, and where it lands
do_what.counted_statements: non-blank, non-comment lines of the quoted block, excluding FORM/ENDFORM/FUNCTION/ENDFUNCTION, the START-OF-SELECTION header, and block closers
do_what.markers: `1.` / `1)` / `-` / `*` / `+` at a line start. Circled digits U+2460-U+246B and the full-width 1。 / 1、 endings are not markdown list markers: CommonMark merges consecutive lines that begin with them into one paragraph, so a first layer 'segmented' that way rendered as a wall of text. 1.3.14 counted them and so validated a shape that displays as nothing
do_what.skill_anchor: 展开成带编号/字段/条件的清单，不要一句话概括
do_what.why: a paragraph cannot hide a missing condition, a list can, and the one-sentence first layer was the shape this rule kept being skipped in. The gate sees the list, never how specific its items are -- one item covering ten statements still passes

violation_kinds.A8-cc: no prose at all inside that window
violation_kinds.A8-pt: prose present inside that window, some labels missing
violation_kinds.A8-list: all labels present, but the first layer is a paragraph instead of a markdown list that renders as one -- includes the 1.1.31 shape of one circled digit per line, which counts as a list here and prints as a single paragraph

forbidden_in_location_labels.why: the skill requires naming the subprogram, not citing a line

mermaid.why: bare < > # terminate a label or start a comment, so the diagram does not render

encoding.why: a truncated multi-byte character renders as U+FFFD and reads as a rendering fault in the finished report; one in exp-1.0.9/with_skill/run3.md went unnoticed for a whole round

escape_residue.why: a report can be valid UTF-8 and still carry an escape written out as text: the writer owed one newline and typed the two characters. enc covers the bytes being wrong; this covers the bytes being right and the intent escaped instead. One shipped report had nine of them, all nine the same shape, and no structural detector saw any of them

tick-n.note: a backtick-wrapped n, r or t immediately followed by another letter -- the mangling that turned each backslash into a backtick, so two newlines read as a backtick-wrapped n then a bare n. Two letters is the floor because a single backticked n is a variable named n, which occurs in prose and in the exemplar. The class stops at n, r and t: measured across the corpus, widening it to every letter starts firing on a backticked variable followed by a word

backslash-escape.scope: prose outside code fences and outside inline backtick spans
backslash-escape.note: a backslash followed by n, r or t with no word character after it, or a \uXXXX or \xNN written out in prose. The lookahead is what keeps a Windows path such as C:\notes out, and exclude_inline_spans is what keeps a quoted \n out -- a quoted escape is the writer naming it, not shipping it

escape_residue.not_repairs: absent from --fix, on purpose. --fix repairs ln and mm because both are substitutions with one right answer; here the answer is a line break in a place only the writer knows, so a repair would have invented prose. esc exits 1 the way enc does
escape_residue.measured: 197 markdown files before shipping: the tick-n shape had zero hits, and the backslash shape outside fences and outside inline spans hit one occurrence in this repository's own release log, which the gate never reads. The tick-n pattern was also measured against the residue instances that reached a shipped report, all of them caught, and against a single backticked letter, which it must not touch. The first pattern tried, a run of two backtick-wrapped n, caught one of the five residue shapes: it reads the shape as repeated `n` units, while the mangling actually turns each backslash into a backtick, so the second n is bare and the run is one backticked letter then a bare one. That is the pattern below

_comment: How to read the checker. Recorded here because the ways of NOT being
checked look like passing, and because these semantics have now been
rewritten three times. The exit-code table SKILL.md taught was written
against an early gate, then against the one that refused a bad source path
instead of passing quietly and dropped the .abap suffix, then against the
one that also refuses a bad report. Byte sizes are deliberately absent:
naming them made this comment go stale every time the file grew, and the
size carried no information the exit-code table does not already state.
Every row below was measured by running the gate, not read off the source.
test_contract_drift.py only asserts the skill_anchor values appear in
SKILL.md. It does not re-derive any of this from report_qc.py, so a change
to main() has to be made here by hand.
1.3.6 changes one word and one entry in this block: row-src joins
source_is_optional.skip_note and diagnostics.needs_source, and exit_codes[2]
records that --fix now writes nothing when a detector crashes. Every other
row is untouched.
1.3.7 changes no row. It changes the shape of the last entry of
conclusion_lines: die() printed its refusal indented two spaces while the
two import-time refusals and checks/contract.py's printed it flush left, so
the same refusal arrived three different ways and a caller matching
conclusion_lines from column 0 missed every refusal that went through die().

1.3.8 changes two things in exit_codes[2] and adds one row. The first is a trigger: --fix now refuses when the write cannot happen, and it is the one trigger where the report was read first, so the opening clause stops saying nothing was inspected and the error line says it was read but nothing was written. The second is a boundary exit_codes[2] used to be true of and is no longer: in --fidelity-only, exit 2 no longer follows a printed verdict, because every report path is validated before any report is read. The new row is directory_as_source: a folder was reporting itself as an unreadable file.

1.3.10 widens two triggers and fixes one recorded message, without adding a trigger. exit_codes[2]'s report-path conditions covered existence only; a directory and a file that does not decode as utf-8 were refused inside the loop, so exit 2 could follow a printed PASS. They are now pre-validated before any report is read, in every mode. directory_as_source.prints now records both role-specific forms instead of the source form alone -- before, a reader looking up the report form found nothing.

1.3.11 widens two triggers and adds nothing. The first is gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set: the trigger text said missing or not parseable, but a contract that parses can still be unusable in the way the guard was written to catch. 1.1.24 moved the derivations under the same guard for a missing key and its _comment recorded that the catch widened to cover every shape json.load can return -- that record was wrong. The presence loop and the derivations were two separate try blocks, so a rule that was present and mistyped still died outside the guard, and the exceptions it raised were not all in the clause: StopIteration from advisories carrying no density row, LookupError from a problem section that is also the last section, re.error from a pattern the contract supplies that does not compile, and TypeError from the joining. Each exited 1 with a traceback, the defect verdict, for a rule set that was only reshaped. The derivations now sit inside the guard, and the catch names those four as well, so every one of them is a refusal on the same error line. The second is exit_codes[2]'s fidelity-only trigger: it said the source is empty, which named the whitespace case only. A source of 500 control bytes is not empty and not blank by .strip(), and a source of nothing but the replacement character passes isprintable(), so both reached the detectors as real sources. Both refuse now, on the trigger's own words. Both changes are refusals that were tracebacks, not new refusals, so the trigger set is the same and only the wording and the scoping moved.

1.3.12 changes two rows and adds no trigger. fix_writes_a_backup described a guard that was narrower than the promise it made. The guard was `if dest == rep and n`, so a backup was owed only when the report was rewritten in place and only when something had been repaired; that left the -o half unmet, because -o names a destination that may already hold a file and replacing it destroyed it on the same run that printed repaired and exited 0. The guard is now a byte comparison, old_bytes != written, so a backup is owed whenever the write would lose something, in place or via -o, and still when a repair that found nothing replaces a foreign file with the report, because those bytes are the file's own. A no-op --fix writes back the same bytes and owes none, which is the property that makes an in-place --fix safe to run twice. The second row is exit_codes[2]'s write trigger, which named a directory only -- the shape that raises IsADirectoryError -- while a .bak that was already a file is the ordinary case, the second --fix over the same report, and it was overwritten without a word. It refuses on any existing path now, file or directory, because both hold a version of the report and neither said so. The destination is called <target> rather than <report>, because in place it is the report and via -o it may be a file that is not. Both changes are a backup or a refusal where there was destruction, and no exit code moves.

exit_codes.0: every report was checked, no shape defect was found, and there is no substantive rewrite -- fidelity SUBSTANTIVE findings also block 0, so a shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exits 1, in every mode; notes may accompany it and never change it
exit_codes.1: the check ran and found defects. Shape mode prints the defect lines first -- the shape prefixes plus one SUBSTA line per fidelity SUBSTANTIVE finding, and N counts both -- then the verdict, then the notes: the verdict is not the last line in shape mode or in --fix, notes follow it. --fidelity-only prints the tier lines first (displayed as SUBSTA and PUNCT-, six characters, truncated from the canonical names), then `FAIL  <name>  (N rewrite(s), M punctuation-only)` or `PASS  <name>` -- or `PASS  <name>  (N punctuation-only)` when the only findings are advisory, the verdict still reads PASS and the exit is still 0, and a reader who matches `PASS  <name>` exactly would miss the count -- and until 1.3.9 only there was the verdict last -- the SUBSTANTIVE note, with its denominator and the wrong-file question, now follows the verdict in --fidelity-only as well. --fix prints `FAIL  <name>  (<what is left> need the model)`, naming the two kinds separately -- `N shape defect(s)`, `N rewrite(s)`, or both joined by ` and ` -- then its notes, and it exits 1 for a rewrite as well: until 1.3.4 --fix returned 0 and printed PASS where shape mode returned 1 for the same report, so 0 meant two different things in two modes. The verdict names the kinds instead of one shared count, because folding shape and rewrite defects into a single N would make the fix look cosmetic while hiding which one is still to fix
exit_codes.2: refused to run, so do not act on what it printed. In every trigger except the --fix write refusal below, nothing was inspected. Triggers, by mode -- the mode matters and the flat list this replaced did not say so: common, the rule set could not be read -- schemas/report-contract.json is missing or not parseable JSON / the gate's own detectors did not load -- scripts/checks/ is absent or a module in it will not parse / no arguments / no .md/.markdown path among the arguments / report path does not exist; plain, more than one source / source path does not exist; --fidelity-only, the source is not exactly one (0 and 2 both refuse) / source does not exist / the source has no analysable content -- empty, whitespace-only, or carrying nothing but control bytes or U+FFFD / the source is not utf-8; --fix, fewer than two paths / -o with no output path; and in all three modes a file that is not utf-8, report or source. Two triggers print no `error` line: no arguments prints the usage text, and --fix with too few paths prints `--fix needs REPORT and SOURCE`. SKILL.md records both. An empty source is NOT a refusal in plain mode -- the shape can still be checked, so it takes a note and returns the shape verdict; that scoping was the second thing the flat list got wrong. 1.3.11 widens that trigger from an empty source to any source with no analysable character and changes no scoping: plain mode still takes the note and returns the shape verdict, and --fidelity-only still refuses. The two detectors-did-not-load triggers arrived with 1.1.0's split of report_qc.py and were missing from this row until 1.3.0: the guard prints `error  cannot load the checks at <scripts dir> (<cause>), so nothing was checked` and exits 2, in every mode, because a missing checks/ otherwise raised ImportError and an unparseable one raised SyntaxError, and both exit 1 -- the defect verdict. Those two are listed first under common because they fire at import, before argv is read, so a mode can never be the thing that decides them. 1.3.1 adds a third, in every mode: an unhandled exception inside the check loop prints `error  internal error checking <report>: <type>: <msg> -- the gate crashed, so treat this report as unchecked, not as defects found` and exits 2 -- that is the event-block IndexError that shipped in 1.1.2, which printed a traceback and exited 1, and read as a FAIL. 1.3.2 restores the rule-set trigger to this row: 1.2.4 added it alongside gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set, and the 1.2.6 rewrite of this string dropped only the wording, so the flat list had silently lost the earliest of the four import-time refusals -- checks/contract.py reads the JSON before anything else in the import block can fail, and a wrong relative path is the cheapest way to reach it. Nothing else in the row changed, and the gate behaves exactly as it did at 1.3.1. 1.3.6 makes the opening clause literal in --fix as well: until then the write sat between the second detector and the three that followed it, so a crash in any of those exited 2 and said nothing had been inspected while the output file was already on disk -- and in place, where the report is usually the only copy, the refusal left a .bak to recover from. All four detectors now run before the write, so a refusal leaves no file behind. 1.3.7 makes the shape of the error line uniform too: die() indented it two spaces while the two import-time refusals printed it flush left, so the same refusal arrived three different ways and a caller matching this row's error line from column 0 missed every refusal that went through die(). The two trigger lists are unchanged. 1.3.8 adds a trigger and makes the opening clause narrower. --fix now refuses when the write cannot happen: error  could not write <path>: <type>: <msg> -- nothing was written, so this run is not a verdict. The triggers are --fix, -o is a directory or a read-only file / <target>.bak is already there, a file or a directory, in place or via -o; and in --fidelity-only a report path does not exist, which is now checked before any report is read. This is the one exit-2 trigger where something WAS inspected: the report was read and its defects were found, and the repair simply could not be saved, so the message says what happened rather than claiming a refusal. That is why the opening clause stopped saying nothing was inspected. Before 1.3.8 these paths raised OSError and printed a traceback with exit 1 -- the defect verdict -- and wrote no file, so the caller went fixing defects that were never found, or looped step 7 forever. The write sat outside run_detector(), the guard the four detectors got in 1.1.3; the pre-flight check covered only the directory of -o, never -o itself, which is why no test could reach it. A refusal here prints no verdict line, because the verdict lines follow the write; the defect lines that ran before it are already above the error line on the same output, so the error line is not the first line the gate printed and nothing was silently dropped. And --fidelity-only: it took several reports and validated them inside its loop, so it printed a PASS and then refused -- exit 2 could follow a printed verdict, and a caller keying on 2 as nothing was inspected discarded a real PASS, while the same call in plain mode refused first and printed nothing. Now every report path is validated before any report is read, as plain mode does. Also directory_as_source: a directory passed as the source used to print is not readable as utf-8, which is a PermissionError wearing an encoding error's clothes and sent a reader hunting for a BOM in a folder. 1.3.10 widens two of the report-path triggers without adding any. A report that is a directory, and a report that does not decode as utf-8, used to be refused inside the loop, after the earlier reports had already printed their verdict, so exit 2 could follow a printed PASS that SKILL.md promised would never happen; both are now pre-validated with existence, in every mode. An -o outside --fix refused here all along, but as more than one source: src, -o, which named the flag as a source file; it now says that --fix goes first on the line. The trigger lists are otherwise unchanged. 1.3.12 widens the .bak trigger and adds none: it named a directory only, which is the shape that raises IsADirectoryError, while a .bak that is already a file -- the ordinary case, the second --fix over the same report -- was overwritten without a word. It refuses on any existing path now, file or directory, because both hold a version of the report and neither said so. The destination is called <target> rather than <report>, because in place it is the report and via -o it may be a file that is not.
exit_codes.why_2_is_separate: an unhandled exception exits 1, which is the code SKILL.md defines as 'the check ran and found defects', and the caller then goes and fixes defects that do not exist, or loops step 7 forever. So every refusal has to arrive through die(), including a decode failure on the report. The report side was bare at three call sites until 1.0.9: a report saved as cp936 -- what an editor's 'save as' gives on a Chinese Windows, the trap SKILL.md warns about for pasted source -- exited 1 with a traceback. The source side was guarded from the start and the rule set has its own try/except at import, so the guarantee covered one of the two files.
exit_codes.measured: 1.0.9: every cell of SKILL.md's per-mode table was run against report_qc.py, all 13 agree, and the six non-utf-8-report cases now exit 2 in all three modes. test_skill.py carries 28 checks for it. 1.3.0: the two detectors-did-not-load triggers were measured the same way, by deleting scripts/checks/ from a copy and by appending an unparseable line to checks/text.py in a copy -- both print the error line above and exit 2. 1.3.1: the detector-crash trigger was measured by reverting the inventory() fix in a copy of the tree and checking a report against a source that declares START-OF-SELECTION -- it prints the error line above and exits 2 instead of raising IndexError and exiting 1. test_skill.py carries that source as a permanent check, asserting both that no traceback is printed and that inventory() still counts all six event blocks as a denominator, so a regression that returns an empty inventory instead of crashing is caught too. 1.3.2: the rule-set trigger was re-measured on a copy of the tree, once with schemas/ removed and once with unparseable JSON written to schemas/report-contract.json -- both print the error line of gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set and exit 2, in every mode. 1.3.5: the detector-crash trigger was re-measured in all three modes at once, by injecting a RuntimeError into report_qc's detectors and running shape mode, --fidelity-only and --fix against the same report -- all three print the error line above and exit 2. Before the fix, --fidelity-only exited 1 with a traceback and --fix exited 1 with a traceback after it had already rewritten the output file, so exit 2 was enforced only in the one branch whose guard had been written. Two regressions were caught by re-running every mode instead of the one that changed: the new guard first swallowed an argument out of report() and broke the shape-mode baseline, which the baseline check caught before anything was packed. test_skill.py now carries nine checks for the guard, one for each of the three assertions in each of the three modes, and fails on --fidelity-only and --fix against the pre-fix tree. The advisory PASS form was measured by moving one space inside a parenthesis in a quoted statement -- SELECT ... INTO @DATA(ls_foo ) -- which the identity check accepts and the flattened substring check rejects, so --fidelity-only prints PASS  <name>  (1 punctuation-only) and exits 0. 1.3.6: the blank-source verdict was measured by pointing the exemplar at a file of spaces and tabs -- 28 defects and exit 1, against PASS with its own source, and an exit-2 refusal from --fidelity-only on the same file. After the fix the same call prints PASS and names what it did not measure, and --fidelity-only still refuses it. test_skill.py carries four checks for the blank source, and one per --fix detector position asserting that no crash position leaves an output file behind; against the pre-fix tree the first of those four fails and all four ordering checks fail. 1.3.7: the refusal shape was measured by taking three die() paths at once -- --fidelity-only with the report as its own source, --fidelity-only with two sources, and --fix into a directory that does not exist -- and asserting each prints its error line from column 0; the two trigger lists above are unchanged, so no new trigger is recorded here. test_skill.py carries one check per path, and fails against the pre-fix tree. 1.3.8: the three write paths were measured by passing -o a directory, passing -o a read-only file, and making <report>.bak an existing directory in place -- all three print the error line above and exit 2, and the report is byte-identical to what it was before, so a refusal leaves nothing behind in every mode. The multi-report refusal was measured by passing one good report and one missing path to --fidelity-only: before the fix it printed PASS for the first and then refused; now it refuses with no verdict printed, and the same call in plain mode still refuses first. The directory trigger was measured in all three modes. 1.3.12 was measured the same way. A 33-byte file named by -o became the 889-byte repaired report with no backup anywhere, and the same call now leaves those 33 bytes at <target>.bak before it writes. Two in-place runs, each repairing something, left 833 bytes at .bak and then 829 with the first copy gone, and the second now refuses with the earlier copy intact and the report byte-identical. A report with one CRLF among fifty-five LFs came out with fifty-six CRLFs and no lone LF, and now comes out break for break, in every combination the test covers. test_skill.py carries 17 checks for the three, and the first two fail against the pre-fix tree.

gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.where: module import, before main() and before every exit-2 guard
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.trigger: schemas/report-contract.json is missing or not parseable JSON, or a rule in it is present but not the type the derivation reads -- see the 1.3.11 note in _comment, which records that the 1.1.24 wording claimed this trigger covered every shape json.load can return
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.prints: error  cannot read the rule set at <path> (<cause>), so nothing was checked
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.why_not_1: an unhandled exception exits 1, which is the defect verdict; refusing by exception is the one false reassurance this script is not allowed to give, arriving through the wrong door

argument_roles.rule: a report is any path ending .md or .markdown; every other path on the command line is a source
argument_roles.why: the previous gate recognised a source by the .abap suffix, so a .txt source was neither read nor announced and was then checked as a report -- a source file with no six sections then failed the gate on defects that were never real
argument_roles.one_source_only: two sources is an error, not a silent 'use the last one', which looks like a successful run while checking one report against nothing

source_is_optional.skip_note: no source recognised, so density, fidelity, fix-mislabel, authz, ext-asset and row-src were not run (pass the ABAP file after the report)
source_is_optional.verdict_still_printed: PASS and exit 0 -- the shape verdict is real, six checks simply did not run

directory_as_source.trigger: a directory is passed where a file is expected, as the source in any mode or as the report in --fidelity-only and --fix
directory_as_source.prints: error  <path> is a directory, not a report file, so nothing was checked; error  <path> is a directory, not a source file, so nothing was compared
directory_as_source.why_not_encoded: a directory raises PermissionError from open(). Until 1.1.23 the OSError clause reported the pair as is not readable as utf-8, which sent a reader looking for a BOM in a folder, so a directory was named on its own. As of 1.1.23 the OSError clause says cannot be read, kept apart from the decode clause, so a denial no longer reads as an encoding error; the directory check stays, because cannot be read says what failed but not what to do, and a directory is the one case where the reader can act

diagnostics.enforcement: note -- never changes the exit code, so the writer has to read them. The one exception is fidelity: its SUBSTANTIVE tier is a defect line, counted in N and in the exit code, not a note, so this row does not cover it. That is advisories[fidelity].enforcement, and the two rows disagreeing is how a reader would read fidelity as advisory-only

gate_io.fence_sorts_first: an unclosed fence swallows the rest of the document, so nothing after it is inspected at all; fixing anything else before fixing that is wasted
conclusion_lines: FAIL  <name>  (N shape defect(s) need the model)
FAIL  <name>  (N shape defect(s) and M rewrite(s) need the model)
gate_io.notes_follow_the_verdict: in shape mode and in --fix the verdict is followed by up to seven notes, so a reader who reads only the last line misses them all -- including the note announcing that five diagnostics never ran. Only --fidelity-only ends on its verdict
gate_io.fix_writes_a_backup: --fix saves the previous text next to the file it is about to replace, as <target>.bak, before it writes, and preserves the report's own CRLF/LF endings break for break. Both destinations owe one: in place the file is the report, usually the only copy, and via -o it may already hold someone else's. The guard is a byte comparison, old_bytes != written, so a backup exists exactly when the write would lose something. That is what makes a no-op --fix safe to run twice -- it writes back the same bytes and owes none -- and what still owes one when a repair that found nothing replaces a foreign file with the report, because those bytes are the file's own and the write loses them. The guard used to be `if dest == rep and n`, so a backup was owed only in place and only when something had been repaired, and an -o over an existing file was overwritten with nothing left to recover from. The endings are carried back one for one rather than one style being chosen for the document: the pass runs on LF text, and each break of the repaired text is the same break of the report, so a report with one CRLF among fifty-five LFs stays that way instead of becoming fifty-six CRLFs under a receipt that said it had repaired nothing. Both writes refuse through die() and exit 2, printing that nothing was written -- exit 1 is the verdict a caller loops on, and a write failure read as one, so the run is never half-repaired -- and a <target>.bak that already exists refuses too, because that copy is the earlier version worth recovering
gate_io.skill_anchor: 退出码是唯一的机器判据

advisories.why: a report can satisfy every rule above and still be a list rather than an analysis

advisories.enforcement: PUNCT-ONLY is a note; SUBSTANTIVE is a defect line counted in N and in the exit code

tiers.SUBSTANTIVE: a defect line, counted in the FAIL total and in the exit code -- it blocks exit 0 in every mode, including the shape-only steps 6 and 7
tiers.PUNCT-ONLY: a note only, never changes the exit code; filtered out of the shape-mode defect count

advisories.display_prefix: the gate prints tier[:6], so the canonical names appear as the six characters SUBSTA and PUNCT-
advisories.note_counts_its_denominator: the SUBSTANTIVE note reads N of M quoted statement(s) rewrite the source, where M is every quoted statement in the report, not only the mismatches. A count with no denominator cannot be read: three rewrites is a few slips in a long report and total fabrication in a short one. The note adds that not one quotation matches the source, and asks whether the source is the one the report was written against, when M equals the number of SUBSTANTIVE findings -- every quotation a rewrite, not one quotation's tokens occurring in the source. That is the one boundary that needs no threshold: a cutoff on identifier count would not separate the cases, since a comments-only file yields 6 identities and an English prose file 20, both non-zero. It has to be SUBSTANTIVE and not all mismatches: PUNCT-ONLY is a quotation whose tokens DO occur in the source, only the punctuation differing, so counting it makes the sentence false in the one configuration that proves the source is the right file. 1.3.7 measured that case -- one punctuation-only and one substantive quotation printed 1 of 2 rewrite the source, and not one quotation matches the source, followed on the next line by a note saying the first differs in punctuation only -- and 1.3.8 changed the condition to the SUBSTANTIVE count. When every quotation is punctuation-only the note is skipped altogether. classify() returns only the mismatches, so both halves read _quote_probes(), one shared probe set, so the count and the mismatches cannot drift apart. 1.3.9 adds the mode scope this row had left out: the note was printed in shape mode and --fix only, because --fidelity-only called classify(), which returns the mismatches and nothing else. So the writer who ran SKILL.md step 6 -- the step whose whole purpose is fidelity -- read neither N of M nor the wrong-file question, in the one mode where they matter most. --fidelity-only now runs fidelity_report, the same path the other two modes use, and all three print the same note
advisories.identity_window_cap: the source's identity windows are enumerated up to 30 tokens per position, because enumerating every window is O(N x W) and uncapped is O(N^2). A probe longer than the cap is not in the set at all, so it cannot be found: before 1.3.8 that read as absent, and since classify() trusts neither classifier and takes their union, the silence became a SUBSTANTIVE even when the quotation was verbatim in the source. Measured over 81 sources and 177092 statements, 8 exceeded the cap, longest 40 tokens, and each one was a SUBSTANTIVE that never cleared -- so steps 6 and 7 looped on a defect that does not exist. Those probes are now searched directly against the source's token sequence, O(N x L) for that one probe instead of the O(N^2) an uncapped pre-computation would cost. The cap still bounds the common case, which is what it was there for.
advisories.why: a fabricated block keeps six sections, three layers and four buckets; nothing structural sees it

fence language is the only admission test, but a proposed fix left in an abap fence is probed against the source and reads as fabricated; the exemption used to be positional and skipped the next sub-step's real quote as well -- 12 of 138 quoted statements uninspected on one report

a program that reads data but never checks authorization is a real question, not automatically a finding: reports run under S_TCODE, so anyone who can execute already may see the output. The note therefore asks rather than asserts, and it stays silent when the source does read data and has an AUTHORITY-CHECK. Scoped to data-reading sources so a program that touches no data is not flagged -- a note nobody reads is worse than no note
advisories.answered_when_report_states: a consequence, not the topic. Naming the absence ('no permission check') is not answering it; the question is what follows from it. Measured on a real report that said '不做权限控制' and was still judged partial for not saying who can then see the data

advisories.why: bitmaps, icons and OData service names live in the target system, not in the source, so naming one as a literal creates a dependency that no compiler and no syntax check can see; the failure appears at run time. Reports the names and the count of TRY/EXCEPTIONS guards in the source, and asks whether each call site is inside one

abap and abap-fix locked in only one direction: a fix left in an abap fence is probed and reads as fabricated, but source pasted into an abap-fix fence is never compared with the source at all, so the language tag could be used to opt a quote out of the check that exists to catch invented quotes
advisories.criterion: contiguity, not membership. An abap-fix fence is called out when its statements, flattened and joined, occur as one adjacent run in the source. The first version asked whether every statement occurs anywhere; it fired five times across nine real reports and all five were genuine fixes (a CALL FUNCTION with EXCEPTIONS added, a DELETE followed by an sy-subrc check, a restructured TRY block) whose lines each exist somewhere in a 1600-line file. Quoting the line you are about to change is legitimate, so membership cannot be the test; a mislabeled quote is a verbatim copy, and a verbatim copy is adjacent.

_comment: Where the checker runs is itself a measured rule, not a style preference.
Run inside generation, the gate costs defect recall: -0.250 at twenty
defects with an exact sign test p=0.0215, and -0.224 at thirty-eight, the
same sign at two resolutions. Run as a separate pass after the analysis
is final, recall returns to a level 0.035 from the no-checker arm while
transcription accuracy is still gained.
What the loop checks makes no difference. An arm that checked only
quotations and an arm that checked everything scored identically, p=1.0.
The cost is the loop occupying writing budget, which section 3 needs. So
the rule is not 'check less' -- it is 'check at a different moment', and a
repair pass may not touch the analysis.
loop_position.magnitude_is_unmeasured: The two deltas below are recorded as measured, but the cells are too few for the effect size: a later three-run arm retracted the point estimate as noise. Direction only -- two resolutions, same sign -- is what the skill teaches, and no percentage appears in SKILL.md.
loop_position.transcription_errors_attribution: The eight errors cited in an earlier draft came from the arm that checked fidelity DURING generation; the post-write arm found two. Neither number belongs to the loop-position rule -- transcription accuracy is the fidelity diagnostic's effect, so SKILL.md now says 'two to eight depending on the arm' and attributes it to the diagnostic.

_comment: Passing a deterministic check licenses only the claim that the shape is
right. It says nothing about whether the analysis is correct, and nothing
about whether anything was missed. archify states this as a rule --
passing one claim never implies the others -- so it is written down here
rather than left to the reader to infer from the tool names.
claim_separation.deterministic_checks_establish: the report has the required shape and quotes source faithfully
claim_separation.requires_a_named_reviewer_for: whether the analysis is correct and what it missed
claim_separation.reviewer_mechanism: scripts/evaluate.py against a frozen defect list in evals/
